title: Sodium-ion Batteries for Grid Storage: 2025 Status Report
text: The National Energy Board's 2025 status report finds that the global market for grid-scale sodium-ion batteries reached USD 1.8 billion in 2025, up from USD 0.6 billion in 2023. Cumulative grid deployments of sodium-ion storage reached 4.2 GWh by mid-2025. Average sodium-ion cell prices fell to USD 58 per kWh in 2025, compared with USD 72 per kWh for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells used in stationary storage. The report identifies three leading manufacturers by shipped capacity: Saltwave Cells, Voltaris Energy and Kestrel Grid. Sodium-ion chemistries avoid lithium, cobalt and nickel, and use aluminium current collectors on both electrodes, which lowers material cost. The board recommends sodium-ion for four-to-eight hour storage where weight matters less than cost.

title: Saltwave Cells opens sodium-ion gigafactory in Pune
text: Saltwave Cells opened a sodium-ion cell factory in Pune with an annual capacity of 12 GWh in its first phase, the company said on Tuesday. The plant makes Saltwave the largest sodium-ion producer outside China by capacity. Rival Voltaris Energy raised USD 310 million in a Series C round in January 2025 to expand production in Chennai. Analysts said falling sodium-ion cell prices were winning orders from utilities for grid storage projects.

title: Saltwave's Pune plant to start at 10 GWh, says state official
text: A state industries department official said Saltwave Cells' Pune plant has an approved first-phase capacity of 10 GWh, lower than the figure cited by the company, with expansion to 20 GWh planned by 2027. The plant qualifies for production-linked incentives for advanced chemistry cells. Saltwave did not respond to a request for comment on the capacity discrepancy.

title: Stationary Storage Outlook 2025
text: Sodium-ion batteries are projected to account for 12% of new stationary storage installations worldwide by 2030 in the stated policies scenario. Leading grid-scale sodium-ion cells now reach a cycle life of 6,000 cycles at 80% depth of discharge, comparable to LFP. The main constraint on growth is the supply of hard carbon anode material, which is currently produced by a small number of suppliers. Falling lithium carbonate prices since 2023 have narrowed the cost advantage of sodium-ion over LFP.

title: Sodium-ion batteries: performance, safety and materials (review)
text: Commercial sodium-ion cells typically achieve gravimetric energy densities of 140 to 160 Wh/kg, below the 170 to 200 Wh/kg of LFP cells. Sodium-ion cells can be stored and shipped at 0% state of charge, which removes the thermal runaway risk during transport. Under nail-penetration and overcharge tests, sodium-ion cells showed lower peak temperatures than LFP. Hard carbon remains the dominant anode material, and its cost depends on precursor biomass and pyrolysis energy.

title: Saltwave Cells launches the world's largest sodium-ion plant
text: Saltwave Cells today launched the world's largest and most advanced sodium-ion battery plant. Our next-generation cells reach an industry-leading 175 Wh/kg and will transform energy storage forever. The plant has a capacity of 12 GWh. Saltwave is proud to lead the sodium revolution.

title: Voltaris Energy signs 500 MWh supply contract with GridCo
text: Voltaris Energy signed a contract to supply 500 MWh of sodium-ion battery systems to GridCo for four-hour storage projects to be commissioned in 2026. Voltaris says its systems are designed for 20-year project lifetimes.

title: Kestrel Grid lands utility partnership for sodium-ion storage
text: Kestrel Grid, a startup building containerised sodium-ion storage systems, announced a partnership with a regional utility to deploy 200 MWh of storage. Kestrel's founders previously built LFP systems and say sodium-ion's performance in cold weather, retaining over 90% capacity at minus 20 degrees Celsius, is a key selling point.

title: Is sodium-ion ready? Costs remain high
text: In 2019, sodium-ion cells cost around USD 120 per kWh in pilot production, well above lithium-ion. Few companies had moved beyond laboratory prototypes, and cycle life rarely exceeded 2,000 cycles.

title: The quiet risks of sodium-ion
text: Sodium-ion has real risks that the hype ignores. Hard carbon anode supply is concentrated, so a shortage could stall factory ramp-ups. Lower energy density means larger, heavier systems, which raises land and installation costs for some projects. And if lithium carbonate prices stay low, LFP could keep its cost edge in many markets.

title: Battery storage for mini-grids in emerging markets
text: Sodium is roughly 1,000 times more abundant in the Earth's crust than lithium, which reduces supply concentration risk for emerging-market buyers. Pilot mini-grid projects in East Africa and South Asia have begun using sodium-ion storage, citing tolerance of high ambient temperatures and lower fire risk.

title: Cheap lithium tests sodium-ion's pitch to utilities
text: Lithium carbonate prices have fallen more than 70% from their 2022 peak, letting LFP storage system prices drop sharply and testing sodium-ion's cost advantage. Executives at Saltwave Cells and Voltaris Energy said utilities still value sodium-ion's safety and cold-weather performance.

title: Sodium-ion battery - Wikipedia
text: A sodium-ion battery is a rechargeable battery that uses sodium ions as charge carriers. It works on the same rocking-chair principle as lithium-ion batteries. Common cathodes include layered oxides, polyanionic compounds and Prussian blue analogues, and hard carbon is the most common anode.

title: New lithium battery recycling plants open in Europe
text: Three lithium-ion battery recycling plants opened in Europe this year, recovering nickel, cobalt and lithium from end-of-life electric vehicle packs using hydrometallurgical processes.
